title: Weather and zero-shot models on GB electricity demand (pre-registered backtest)

primary_sources.paraphrase: Archived report (MIT, 12 Nov 2026): day-ahead GB national demand, 960-day backtest. Three zero-shot models and a weekly-lag regression got the same ECMWF forecast weather. Weather cut error 34% for the regression, 32% Chronos-2, 23% Timestral, 6% TimesFM 2.5. Plan frozen 10 Nov 2026 before scoring. Possible training overlap is acknowledged.

Public MIT repository with plans, lock files, deviation log and results. Earlier no-weather study (1,035 days): error ratio to the regression 0.928 Chronos-2, 0.910 Timestral, 1.009 TimesFM 2.5. Weights are fetched at pinned revisions.

Results note: 960 daily origins, MAE in MW. With/without-weather ratios 0.658 regression, 0.683 Chronos-2, 0.773 Timestral, 0.941 TimesFM 2.5, all passing at 0.0125. Both with weather, model over regression: Chronos-2 0.966 (0.931-1.001), Timestral 1.074 (1.034-1.115), TimesFM 2.5 1.453 (1.394-1.510). No MAPE.

Plan agreed 8 Nov 2026 and amended 9 Nov. The only confirmatory test is each forecaster's error with weather over without (four one-sided tests at 0.0125). The model-versus-regression comparison with weather is not confirmatory. Forecast weather is the ECMWF 00 UTC run of the day before; temperature, wind and solar.

Apache-2.0 model card: zero-shot, about 120M parameters, takes past and known-future covariates, loaded with chronos-forecasting 2.0 or later; CPU said to be supported. Links a paper dated 17 Oct 2025; the weights' own release or commit date is not shown.

claims.text: Given the same forecast weather, the best zero-shot model (Chronos-2) has about 3% lower error than the weekly-lag regression, with a 90% interval that reaches 1.0: roughly a tie. This comparison was descriptive, not a confirmatory test.
claims.metric: MAE ratio, model with weather / regression with weather
claims.dataset: GB national electricity demand, half-hourly, 16 Mar 2024 to 31 Oct 2026

claims.text: With the same weather the other two zero-shot models are worse than the regression: Timestral 1.074 (1.034-1.115) and TimesFM 2.5 1.453 (1.394-1.510).
claims.metric: MAE ratio, model with weather / regression with weather
claims.dataset: GB national electricity demand, half-hourly, 16 Mar 2024 to 31 Oct 2026

claims.text: Weather improves the regression: error with weather is 0.658 of error without (0.631-0.686), a pre-registered confirmatory test.
claims.metric: MAE ratio, with weather / without weather
claims.dataset: GB national electricity demand, half-hourly, 16 Mar 2024 to 31 Oct 2026

claims.metric: MAE ratio, with weather / without weather

relevance.rationale: Electric load at sub-daily resolution (half-hourly national GB demand, not hourly PJM zones), so target 3. Horizon is day-ahead, not a week, so 2. Forecast weather is given as a known-future input to every forecaster, so 3; the study uses temperature, wind and solar where our spec requires temperature only.

label: ACCEPT_RUN
label_reason: On target (electric load, known-future forecast weather, zero-shot models against a regression given the same weather) with a Zenodo record, a public repository, a dated plan and a results note that carry the numbers; the model it finds best, Chronos-2, has public Apache-2.0 weights and can be run with temperature on our benchmark now. Evidence is moderate, not strong: the weather-helps result is pre-registered and confirmatory, but the rough tie with the regression (0.966, interval 0.931 to 1.001) is descriptive, from one author, day-ahead on GB data, with no independent replication found in one search. Training overlap is marked low for our own run only because the Chronos-2 paper (17 Oct 2025) predates our scored window; the weights' commit date was not found, and the study itself says its backtest may overlap the models' training data.
implementation_hint: Chronos-2 with temperature through the direct adapter models/chronos2.py (chronos-forecasting package), weights repository huggingface.co/amazon/chronos-2, compared with the temperature-only regression. Timestral (mistralai/Timestral-209M) can run through models_ff/run_ff.py; TimesFM 2.5 with covariates (google/timesfm-2.5-200m-pytorch) needs models_ff/timesfm25_xreg.py. Horizon mismatch to state: source is day-ahead, ours is 168 h.

receipt.claimed: Given the same forecast weather, Chronos-2's error is 0.966 of a weekly-lag regression's (90% interval 0.931 to 1.001) on GB national demand: a rough tie.
receipt.horizon_mismatch: The study is day-ahead on GB national half-hourly demand with temperature, wind and solar and a regression with 2-day and 7-day lags; ours is a week ahead (168 h) on two PJM zones with temperature only and a 7-day lag.
